title: Whole grid payload under public RSA moduli
question: Does the entire 256-byte LP2-49–51 payload produce a valid PKCS#1 or PSS frame when raised to candidate public exponents under Cicada PGP moduli?
reader_question: Could the number-grid bytes be an RSA block?
summary: The exact public-source E-01 replay found no structure in 162 valid checks under two 4096-bit PGP moduli. The 2013 modulus is too small for a whole 256-byte input.
finding: Zero strict or loose structural matches in 162 valid RSA public-power checks; 12 source encodings excluded because s≥n. Original planted signature controls and 10,000 random-block controls passed.
limitations: Only three pinned payload readings, two valid PGP moduli, source encodings, three exponents and three structural predicates. Public exponentiation cannot decrypt an RSA ciphertext. The 432-bit 2013 modulus admits no whole-payload input.
next_steps: A different RSA proposal must specify which bytes form a block, modulus, exponent or private-key operation, encoding, and structural success criterion before testing.

scope.representation: Three pinned 256-byte readings of the printed base-60 grid as one complete value; two 4096-bit published PGP moduli, with the 432-bit 2013 modulus checked for fit.
scope.procedure: Replay pinned E-01 public exponentiation and PKCS#1 v1.5 signature/encryption plus PSS padding checks on valid endian/alignment representations, exponents 65537, 3 and 17.
scope.parameters: 3 payloads; 2 usable PGP moduli; 3 valid encodings per PGP modulus; 3 exponents; 3 structural predicates = 162 evaluated matcher rows. Twelve source encodings excluded for s≥n, including every 2013-modulus case.
scope.exclusions: Private-key RSA decryption, 54-byte windows within the payload, other key pairs, other padding or payload readings.

review.reviewer: Independent PGP packet fingerprint and modulus extraction, all 162 public-power rows and structural controls

reproduction.environment: Python 3 plus cryptography for original planted-control replay; independent checker uses standard library.

visuals.caption: Only the two 4096-bit moduli admitted whole-payload RSA inputs; neither produced padding structure.
